Bristol families: two proper days out without the usual entry bill 🧡

🌳 TYNTESFIELD, WRAXALL
Free entry Monday 14–Sunday 20 September. Woodland wandering and a grand house to explore. Estate: 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm. No booking for an ordinary family visit.

Budget £5 for non-member parking: that’s the standard September rate, and the event doesn’t promise free parking. House hours are shorter—on Monday 14 September, 10.30am–3.30pm. Pushchairs can’t go inside the house; paths include slopes and gravel, with a mobility shuttle available.

🌿 DYRHAM PARK, NEAR BATH
Free entry AND parking Thursday 17–Saturday 19 September, 10am–5pm; last entry 4pm. No booking. Parkland, a play area and the house, which opens at 11.30am. Some ground is steep and uneven; assistance dogs only.

Both welcome families. Our pick for ages 0–12 with a grown-up; choose a short wander for little legs. Food and optional extras cost more. Dyrham’s free-entry dates do NOT include Sunday 20 September.

National Trust dates and visiting details:
Tyntesfield: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield/events/181b773f-1fc7-4a87-8f4b-41c89c2dd4c8
Dyrham: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/dyrham-park/events/94f2b171-9191-4b0e-a234-810e59b3fe3f

Save the dates, and follow @donext_bristol for more local family plans.

## Friday social roundup — recheck before use

Target: Friday 18 September 15:30 UK. Not scheduled. Retire before Saturday 19 September 10:00. Recheck all four sources and replace anything cancelled or unavailable. Avoid another standalone free-estates post this week.

Bristol, choose your kind of weekend: woods, songs or a little making 🧡

For 19–20 September:

• Tyntesfield: free estate entry both days, 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm. Budget £5 for standard non-member parking; check house hours separately.
• Dyrham Park: free entry and parking on SATURDAY only, 10am–5pm, last entry 4pm. No booking; some steep paths.
• Sea Shanty Shout: free music at Great Eastern Hall, Brunel Square, noon–6pm both days. No booking. This is not entry to the ship.
• Arnold Art Cart at Arnolfini: free self-led family making, 11am–6pm both days, second floor. Not a staffed workshop; materials depend on availability.

Children need a grown-up. Our picks suit a mix of ages 0–12; the music and art stops are especially worth considering from around 3 upwards. Choose one or two, not a marathon.

Dates and access: National Trust Tyntesfield and Dyrham event pages; bristoldockyards.org/whats-on/bristol-sea-shanty-shout; arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/

## Friday weekend-brief email — UNSENT

Subject: Bristol: free-entry woods, sea songs and a rainy-day making stop

Preheader: Four options for 19–20 September, with the Saturday-only offer made clear.

Hi Bristol,

For fresh air, [Tyntesfield](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield/events/181b773f-1fc7-4a87-8f4b-41c89c2dd4c8) has free estate entry on both weekend days, 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm. Budget £5 for standard non-member parking. [Dyrham](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/dyrham-park/events/94f2b171-9191-4b0e-a234-810e59b3fe3f) includes free parking too, but only on Saturday 19: 10am–5pm, last entry 4pm. Neither needs family pre-booking; both have sloping paths and separate house hours.

Prefer a short city stop? [Sea Shanty Shout](https://www.bristoldockyards.org/whats-on/bristol-sea-shanty-shout) is free at Great Eastern Hall, Brunel Square, noon–6pm on Saturday and Sunday, with no booking. It isn’t on the ship. Or use the free [Arnold Art Cart](https://arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/) at Arnolfini, second floor, 11am–6pm: self-led making, not a supervised class.

All children need an adult. We’d choose the city stops particularly for ages 3–12, with help for younger makers; that’s our suggestion, not an admission restriction. Optional food and purchases are extra.

## Weekday subscriber email — UNSENT

Intended Monday 14 September; retire before Wednesday 16 September 10:45. Recheck before any later use.

Subject: Bristol: three small ways out this week

Preheader: A woodland wander, a making table and songs for the smallest ones.

Hi Bristol,

With little ones at home, [Tyntesfield’s free-entry week](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield/events/181b773f-1fc7-4a87-8f4b-41c89c2dd4c8) offers an outdoor option through Sunday 20 September. The estate opens 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm; standard non-member parking is £5. No ordinary family booking; choose a short route on its sloping paths.

From Tuesday 15 September, [Arnolfini’s free Art Cart](https://arnolfini.org.uk/whatson/arnold-art-cart/) is another small option: second floor, 11am–6pm Tuesday–Sunday. Self-led materials for families, best with adult help; it is not available on Monday. Older children could visit after school.

For ages 0–3, [Central Library’s rhyme session](https://www.bristol.gov.uk/residents/libraries-and-archives/services-for-children-and-young-people/baby-bounce-and-rhyme-and-storytime-sessions) is listed on Wednesday 16 September at 10.45am. Free, no booking, around 20 minutes; older siblings welcome. This is a regular timetable, so confirm before a special journey.
